chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, decides to honor a servant but the servant has sins with Him, He afflicts him with illness; if not that, He afflicts him with need; and if not that, He intensifies the severity of his death. And when He decides to humble a servant who has a good deed with Him, He cures his body; if not that, He expands his livelihood; and if not that, He makes death easy for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind a believer's illness or wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the divine wisdom behind afflictions and ease in the life of believers. When Allah wishes to honor a servant with sins, He uses illness, poverty, or a difficult death as means of expiation. Conversely, when He wishes to humble a servant with good deeds, He grants them health, wealth, or an easy death, so that their good deeds are not exhausted by worldly blessings.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 11. It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) (a.s) said:

“When Allah decides to honor a servant but the servant has committed sins, He afflicts him with an ailment. If not that, He puts him in need; and if not that, He intensifies the severity of his death (in order that his sins may be forgiven). And when He decides to disgrace a person who has done some good, He bestows him with well-being. If not that, He amplifies his livelihood; and if not that, He makes his death easy.”
